## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Puṭabhattajātaka* (Ja 223), rendered in English as *The Meal-Packet*, belongs to the Jātaka collection of the Pali canon [SuttaCentral]. In the frame narrative preserved in the commentary, the Buddha related this story while residing at Jetavana about a landed proprietor (*kuṭumbika*) of Sāvatthī [SuttaCentral; Fausböll 1879]. In the story of the past, a queen was neglected by the king who left her to starve; the Bodhisatta, acting as a wise minister (*paṇḍitāmacca*), intervened and spoke corrective verses beginning with *Namo namantassa, bhaje bhajantaṁ* (“Honour for honour”), leading the king to repent [SuttaCentral; Anandajoti 2010; Fausböll 1879]. At the conclusion of the teaching, the married couple established themselves in the fruit of stream-entry (*sotāpatti*) [Fausböll 1879].
SuttaCentral notes the *Pakkagodhajātaka* (Ja 333) as a canonical passage-level parallel to this discourse [SuttaCentral]. In machine-assisted textual analysis, DharmaNexus records Pali-internal text reuse across multiple sections of the *Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā* (parts 2 and 3) [DharmaNexus]. Furthermore, DharmaNexus aligns passages of Ja 223 with the Buddhist Sanskrit *Mahāvastu-avadāna* with high similarity scores [DharmaNexus].
